prompt: A submarine dives to $-250$ ft, then rises $75$ ft. **How far from sea level** is the submarine now?
hint: This takes two steps. Find where the submarine ends up, then ask how far that position is from sea level, which is $0$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try smaller numbers: dive to $-5$ ft and rise $2$ ft. You end at $-3$ ft, which is $3$ ft from sea level. Use the same two steps here.
This takes two steps. Find where the submarine ends up, then ask how far that position is from sea level, which is $0$.
The new position is $-250 + 75$. Because $75$ is less than $250$, the submarine is still below sea level. The distance from sea level is the absolute value of the position.
$-250 + 75 = -175$ and $|-175| = 175$, so the submarine is $175$ ft from sea level.

explanation: Rising $75$ ft means adding $75$ to the starting position: $-250 + 75$.
The rise is smaller than the depth, so the submarine stays below sea level at $-(250 - 75) = -175$ ft.
Sea level is $0$, so the distance from sea level is the absolute value of the position: $|-175|$.
$|-175| = 175$, so the submarine is $175$ ft from sea level.
